pubs.factsheet_faq.source: IRS reliance page (last reviewed 5 December 2025), citing Reg. § 1.6662-4(d) — https://www.irs.gov/newsroom/general-overview-of-taxpayer-reliance-on-guidance-published-in-the-internal-revenue-bulletin-and-faqs

pubs.informal_guidance.value: forms, instructions, publications and IRS.gov webpages — they do not apply the law to taxpayer-specific facts, may not reflect special rules or exceptions, have not been published in the Internal Revenue Bulletin, and "will not be relied on, used, or cited as precedents by Service personnel in the disposition of cases"
pubs.informal_guidance.source: IRS, "General overview of taxpayer reliance on guidance published in the Internal Revenue Bulletin and FAQs," page last reviewed 5 December 2025 — https://www.irs.gov/newsroom/general-overview-of-taxpayer-reliance-on-guidance-published-in-the-internal-revenue-bulletin-and-faqs

pubs.law_controls.value: if information in informal guidance or an FAQ turns out to be an inaccurate statement of the law as applied to a particular taxpayer's case, the law controls the taxpayer's tax liability — only guidance published in the Internal Revenue Bulletin has precedential value
pubs.law_controls.source: IRS, "General overview of taxpayer reliance on guidance published in the Internal Revenue Bulletin and FAQs," page last reviewed 5 December 2025 — https://www.irs.gov/newsroom/general-overview-of-taxpayer-reliance-on-guidance-published-in-the-internal-revenue-bulletin-and-faqs

pubs.reliance_penalty.value: a taxpayer who shows reliance in good faith that was reasonable on all the facts and circumstances will not be subject to a penalty carrying a reasonable cause standard — including a negligence or other accuracy-related penalty — to the extent the reliance results in an underpayment
pubs.reliance_penalty.source: IRS reliance page (last reviewed 5 December 2025), citing Reg. § 1.6664-4(b) — https://www.irs.gov/newsroom/general-overview-of-taxpayer-reliance-on-guidance-published-in-the-internal-revenue-bulletin-and-faqs

pubs.status.value: IRS publications explain the law in plain language, highlight changes, give examples of IRS positions and include worksheets — but they are nonbinding on the IRS, do not necessarily cover all positions for an issue, and "should not be cited to sustain a position"

qbi.deduction.value: the lesser of the combined qualified business income amount or 20 percent of the excess of taxable income over net capital gain — subject to the IRC § 199A(i) minimum

qbi.entity_scope.value: available to a taxpayer other than a corporation — so to a sole proprietor and to an owner of a partnership or S corporation on their share, but not to a C corporation and not on wages

qbi.exclusions.value: reasonable compensation paid to the taxpayer, IRC § 707(c) guaranteed payments, § 707(a) service payments to the extent regulations provide, and — new for 2026 — any amount for which the § 224(a) qualified tips deduction is allowable
qbi.exclusions.source: IRC § 199A(c)(4)(A)-(D), subparagraph (D) added by Pub. L. 119-21 § 70201(d) — https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/199A

qbi.minimum_deduction.value: the deduction is the greater of the amount otherwise determined or $400, for a taxpayer with at least $1,000 of aggregate qualified business income from active qualified trades or businesses in which they materially participate within IRC § 469(h) — both figures indexed from 2027
qbi.minimum_deduction.source: IRC § 199A(i)(1)(A), (B), (2)(A), (B), added by Pub. L. 119-21 § 70105; Rev. Proc. 2025-32 § 2.12 — https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/199A

qbi.per_business_amount.value: for each qualified trade or business, the lesser of 20 percent of its qualified business income or the greater of 50 percent of its W-2 wages, or 25 percent of those wages plus 2.5 percent of the unadjusted basis immediately after acquisition of all qualified property

qbi.permanence.value: permanent — the former IRC § 199A(i) sunset for taxable years beginning after 2025 was replaced by Pub. L. 119-21 § 70105 with the minimum deduction, at the same address
qbi.permanence.source: IRC § 199A(i), as amended by Pub. L. 119-21 § 70105 — https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/199A

qbi.phase_in_range.value: the limitation phases in between the threshold and $553,500 joint, $276,775 married filing separately, $276,750 otherwise — a range of $150,000 joint and $75,000 otherwise, doubled from the original by Pub. L. 119-21

qbi.phase_in_width.value: $75,000, or $150,000 on a joint return — raised from $50,000 and $100,000 for taxable years beginning after 31 December 2025
qbi.phase_in_width.source: IRC § 199A(b)(3)(B), (d)(3) as amended by Pub. L. 119-21 § 70105(a)(1), (a)(2), (c) — https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/199A

qbi.specified_service.value: a specified service trade or business — health, law, accounting, actuarial science, performing arts, consulting, athletics, financial services, brokerage services, any trade or business whose principal asset is the reputation or skill of its employees or owners, and investing, trading or dealing in securities, partnership interests or commodities — is excluded once income passes the phase-in range

qbi.threshold.value: $403,500 on a joint return, $201,775 married filing separately, $201,750 for all other returns — below which the wage and property limitation does not apply at all

qbi.thresholds.value: $403,500 on a joint return, $201,775 for a married individual filing separately and $201,750 in any other case, with the phase-in range running to $553,500, $276,775 and $276,750 respectively

qdi.holding_period.value: more than 60 days during the 121-day period beginning 60 days before the ex-dividend date, counting the day of disposition but not the day of acquisition; more than 90 days in a 181-day period for preferred stock dividends attributable to a period exceeding 366 days

recapture.1245.value: ordinary income equal to the excess over adjusted basis of the lower of the recomputed basis or — on a sale, exchange or involuntary conversion — the amount realized, or on any other disposition the fair market value; recognized notwithstanding any other provision of the subtitle

recapture.1245_property.value: property that is or has been subject to the depreciation allowance under IRC § 167 and is either personal property or certain tangible property other than a building or its structural components

recapture.1245_recomputed_basis.value: adjusted basis plus all adjustments reflected in it for depreciation or amortization allowed or allowable — with deductions under IRC §§ 179, 179B to 179E, 181, 190, 193 and 194 treated as amortization, and "allowed" substituted where the taxpayer proves less was taken than was allowable

recapture.1250.value: the applicable percentage — 100 percent for all section 1250 property outside four named housing categories — of the lower of the additional depreciation attributable to periods after 31 December 1975 or the gain

recapture.1250_additional_depreciation.value: for property held more than one year, only the depreciation adjustments in excess of what the straight line method would have produced — so where straight line was used, there is none

recapture.1250_modern_property.value: nil in practice — the applicable depreciation method is the straight line method for nonresidential real property and for residential rental property, so no additional depreciation arises to recapture

recapture.exceptions.value: neither section applies to a disposition by gift or, except as IRC § 691 provides, to a transfer at death; on a § 332, 351, 361, 721 or 731 transfer or a § 1031 or § 1033 disposition, recapture is capped by the gain actually recognised

recapture.unrecaptured_1250_gain.value: taxed at 25 percent — the long-term capital gain that would have been ordinary income if § 1250(b)(1) included all depreciation and the applicable percentage were 100 percent; a rate ceiling on capital gain, not a recharacterisation

records.274d_adequate.value: an account book, diary, log, statement of expense, trip sheet or similar record, together with documentary evidence, which in combination establish each required element

records.274d_categories.value: 3 — traveling expenses under § 162 or § 212 (including meals and lodging while away from home), expenses for gifts, and listed property as defined in § 280F(d)(4)

records.274d_elements.value: 4 — the amount of the expense or other item; the time and place of the travel or the date and description of the gift; the business purpose; and the business relationship to the taxpayer of the person receiving the benefit

records.6001_standard.value: permanent books of account or records, including inventories, sufficient to establish the amount of gross income, deductions, credits, or other matters required to be shown on the return

records.general_retention.value: as long as the period of limitations for the return runs; employment tax records at least 4 years after the tax is due or paid, whichever is later
records.general_retention.source: IRC § 6001; IRS Pub. 583, How Long To Keep Records (page reviewed 30 April 2026)

records.keep.claim.value: 3 years from the date the original return was filed, or 2 years from the date the tax was paid, whichever is later, where a claim for credit or refund is filed after the return
records.keep.claim.source: IRS, How long should I keep records? (irs.gov, Small Businesses and Self-Employed), read 19 August 2026 — https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/how-long-should-i-keep-records

records.keep.default.value: 3 years, where none of the longer periods applies
records.keep.default.source: IRS, How long should I keep records? (irs.gov, Small Businesses and Self-Employed), read 19 August 2026 — https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/how-long-should-i-keep-records

records.keep.employment.value: at least 4 years after the date the tax becomes due or is paid, whichever is later
records.keep.employment.source: IRS, How long should I keep records? (irs.gov, Small Businesses and Self-Employed), read 19 August 2026 — https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/how-long-should-i-keep-records

records.keep.indefinite.value: indefinitely, where no return is filed or a fraudulent return is filed
records.keep.indefinite.source: IRS, How long should I keep records? (irs.gov, Small Businesses and Self-Employed), read 19 August 2026 — https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/how-long-should-i-keep-records

records.keep.omission.value: 6 years, where unreported income exceeds 25% of the gross income shown on the return
records.keep.omission.source: IRS, How long should I keep records? (irs.gov, Small Businesses and Self-Employed), read 19 August 2026 — https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/how-long-should-i-keep-records

records.keep.worthless.value: 7 years, for a claim for a loss from worthless securities or a bad debt deduction
records.keep.worthless.source: IRS, How long should I keep records? (irs.gov, Small Businesses and Self-Employed), read 19 August 2026 — https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/how-long-should-i-keep-records

records.retention_standard.value: kept at all times available for inspection by authorized internal revenue officers or employees, and retained so long as the contents may become material in the administration of any internal revenue law

recovery.reporting_floor.value: $10 or more of refunds, credits or offsets of State or local income taxes for an individual in a calendar year

recovery.tax_benefit_rule.value: a recovery is excluded from gross income to the extent the amount deducted in the earlier year did not reduce the tax imposed by chapter 1

refund.baddebt_period.value: 7 years from the date prescribed for filing the return for the year the claim relates to

refund.claim_period.value: 3 years from the time the return was filed or 2 years from the time the tax was paid, whichever is later; 2 years from payment where no return was filed

refund.consent_tail.value: not before 6 months after the assessment period agreed under § 6501(c)(4) expires

refund.direct_deposit_limit.value: 3 refunds electronically deposited into a single financial account or pre-paid debit card; the fourth and subsequent refunds convert to a paper check
refund.direct_deposit_limit.source: IRS, "Direct deposit limits," page last reviewed 30 September 2025 — https://www.irs.gov/refunds/direct-deposit-limits

refund.disability_suspension.value: suspended while an individual is financially disabled — unable to manage financial affairs through a medically determinable impairment expected to result in death or lasting at least 12 continuous months

refund.eitc_actc_hold.value: no credit or refund may be made before the 15th day of the second month following the close of the taxable year where the earned income credit or the refundable child tax credit is claimed

refund.ftc_period.value: 10 years from the date prescribed for filing the return for the year the foreign taxes were actually paid or accrued

refund.lookback.three_year.value: tax paid within the 3 years immediately preceding the claim, plus any period of extension of time for filing

refund.lookback.two_year.value: tax paid within the 2 years immediately preceding the claim

refund.nol_period.value: 3 years after the due date, including extensions, of the return for the loss year that produces the carryback, or the § 6511(c) period, whichever expires later

reg.authority.value: except where the authority is expressly given to someone outside the Treasury Department, the Secretary prescribes all needful rules and regulations for the enforcement of the title, including those needed by reason of any alteration of law

reg.forms.value: the most important internal revenue rules are issued as regulations and Treasury decisions, prescribed by the Commissioner and approved by the Secretary or delegate; they are prepared in the Office of the Chief Counsel, approved by the Commissioner, then forwarded to the Secretary or delegate for final approval

reg.notice_and_comment.value: where 5 U.S.C. § 553 requires it, general notice of proposed rules is published in the Federal Register, stating the time, place and nature of the public rulemaking proceedings, the authority under which the rule is proposed, and either the terms or substance of the proposed rule or a description of the subjects and issues involved

reg.small_business_review.value: after publication of a proposed or temporary regulation the Secretary submits it to the Chief Counsel for Advocacy of the Small Business Administration, who has 4 weeks to comment on its impact on small business; those comments must be considered before a superseding final regulation is prescribed

reg.temporary.value: any temporary regulation must also be issued as a proposed regulation, and expires within 3 years after the date of issuance

reit.qbi_share.value: 20 percent of the aggregate of qualified REIT dividends and qualified publicly traded partnership income, added to the combined qualified business income amount without any wage or property limitation

residency.closer_connection.value: presence on fewer than 183 days in the current year, together with a tax home in and a closer connection to a foreign country

residency.exempt_individuals.value: 4 categories whose days are not counted — a foreign government-related individual, a teacher or trainee, a student, and a professional athlete temporarily present to compete in a charitable sports event

residency.spt_current_year.value: at least 31 days of presence in the United States during the calendar year

residency.spt_weighted.value: 183 days or more, counting each day of the current year in full, one-third of each day in the first preceding year, and one-sixth of each day in the second preceding year

rmd.aggregation.value: computed separately for each IRA but satisfiable from any one or more of them; separately again for section 403(b) contracts, which aggregate only among themselves; and never across the two, nor with a Roth IRA — an employer plan under section 401(a) is satisfied from that plan alone

rmd.applicable_age.value: 73 for an individual who attains age 72 after 31 December 2022 and age 73 before 1 January 2033; 75 for an individual who attains age 74 after 31 December 2032

rmd.computation.value: the account balance as of 31 December of the preceding calendar year, divided by the applicable denominator from the Uniform Lifetime Table for the owner's age on their birthday in the distribution year — never more than the whole balance on the date of distribution

rmd.first_year_deferral.value: the distribution for the first distribution calendar year may be made on or before April 1 of the following year; every later year's must be made by 31 December of that year — so deferring puts two years' distributions into one

rmd.not_rollover_eligible.value: a required minimum distribution cannot be rolled over or converted; the first dollars distributed in a year for which one is due are the required amount

rmd.required_beginning_date.value: April 1 of the calendar year following the later of the year the employee attains the applicable age or the year the employee retires — but the retirement leg is unavailable to a 5-percent owner and unavailable for IRAs, where the age year always governs

rmd.roth_exempt.value: no lifetime distribution is required from a Roth IRA or, since the amendment of IRC § 402A(d)(5), from a designated Roth account in an employer plan — the requirement attaches only after death

rmd.uniform_lifetime_divisors.value: 26.5 at age 73, 25.5 at 74, 24.6 at 75, 20.2 at 80 and 1.0 at 120 or older — with a joint and last survivor denominator instead where the sole beneficiary is a spouse more than 10 years younger

roth.contribution_phaseout.value: $242,000 to $252,000 on a joint return, $153,000 to $168,000 for a single filer or head of household, and an unindexed $0 to $10,000 for a married individual filing separately

roth.conversion_5year_recapture.value: a distribution allocable to a conversion within the 5-taxable-year period beginning with the taxable year of that conversion is subjected to IRC § 72(t) as if it were includible in gross income, limited to the amount the conversion put into income

roth.conversion_72t.value: does not apply — IRC § 72(t) is switched off for the conversion itself, however large the amount included in gross income

roth.conversion_inclusion.value: any amount that would be includible in gross income were it not part of a qualified rollover contribution — so the pre-tax portion of the converted amount, and nothing else

roth.conversion_income_limit.value: none — the modified adjusted gross income ceiling and the joint-filing requirement that once barred converting were struck by Pub. L. 109-222 § 512(a), effective for taxable years beginning after 2009
roth.conversion_income_limit.source: IRC § 408A(c)(3)(B) and the 2006 amendment and effective-date notes (Pub. L. 109-222, § 512(a), (c)) — https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/408A

roth.conversion_magi_disregard.value: disregarded — an amount included in gross income under IRC § 408A(d)(3) is not taken into account in the modified adjusted gross income that limits a regular Roth contribution

roth.conversion_one_per_year.value: does not apply — the one-rollover-per-year limit of IRC § 408(d)(3)(B) is expressly disregarded for a qualified rollover contribution from a traditional IRA to a Roth IRA

roth.no_lifetime_rmd.value: IRC § 401(a)(9)(A) and the incidental death benefit requirements do not apply to a Roth IRA before the owner's death, notwithstanding IRC § 408(a)(6) and (b)(3)

roth.ordering.value: contributions first to the extent of aggregate contributions, taking regular contributions before qualified rollover contributions, and those on a first-in first-out basis — earnings last

roth.qualified_distribution.value: made after the 5-taxable-year period beginning with the first taxable year for which a contribution was made to any Roth IRA, AND on or after age 59½, on or after death, on account of disability within IRC § 72(m)(7), or as a qualified special purpose distribution

roth.recharacterization_conversions.value: not available — IRC § 408A(d)(6)(A) does not apply to a qualified rollover contribution to which subsection (d)(3) applies, including a conversion, for taxable years beginning after 2017
roth.recharacterization_conversions.source: IRC § 408A(d)(6)(B)(iii), added by Pub. L. 115-97 § 13611(a), effective per § 13611(b) — https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/408A

roth.recharacterization_deadline.value: a trustee-to-trustee transfer accompanied by the net income allocable to the contribution, made on or before the due date for the taxable year including extensions — with an automatic further 6 months from the unextended due date where the return was timely filed

royalty.patent_transfer.value: a transfer of all substantial rights to a patent by a holder, other than by gift, inheritance or devise, is a sale of a capital asset held for more than one year — even where payments are periodic or contingent on productivity or use

salt.cap.value: $40,400 for a taxable year beginning in 2026, halved for a married individual filing separately — rising by 1 percent a year through 2029 and reverting to $10,000 for taxable years beginning after 2029
salt.cap.source: IRC § 164(b)(7)(A)(ii)-(iv) as added by Pub. L. 119-21 § 70120(b) — https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/164

salt.phasedown.value: reduced by 30 percent of modified adjusted gross income above $505,000 for 2026, halved for a married individual filing separately, but never reduced below $10,000

savers.thresholds.value: on a joint return, 50 percent up to $48,500 of adjusted gross income, 20 percent to $52,500, 10 percent to $80,500 and nothing above; head of household $36,375 / $39,375 / $60,375; all others $24,250 / $26,250 / $40,250

savingsbond.exclusion_phaseout.value: begins at modified adjusted gross income of $101,800, or $152,650 on a joint return, and is complete at $116,800 or $182,650

savingsbond.qualification.value: a bond issued after 31 December 1989, at discount under 31 U.S.C. § 3105, to an individual who had attained age 24 before the date of issuance

scholarship.qualified_expenses.value: tuition and fees required for enrollment or attendance, and fees, books, supplies and equipment **required for courses of instruction** — room, board and travel are outside it however necessary they are

scholarship.service_portion.value: any portion representing payment for teaching, research or other services is included, with exceptions only for the National Health Service Corps Scholarship Program, the Armed Forces Health Professions Scholarship and Financial Assistance program, and a comprehensive student work-learning-service program at a work college

sd.aged_or_blind.value: an additional $1,650, increased to $2,050 where the individual is also unmarried and not a surviving spouse

sd.dependent.value: the greater of $1,350, or the sum of $450 and the individual's earned income

sd.mfj.value: $32,200 for married individuals filing joint returns and surviving spouses

sd.mfs.value: $16,100 for married individuals filing separate returns

sd.single.value: $16,100 for unmarried individuals other than surviving spouses and heads of household

se.additional_medicare_threshold.value: $250,000 on a joint return, half that for a married taxpayer filing separately, and $200,000 in any other case — reduced, but not below zero, by wages taken into account for the corresponding FICA tax

se.base_reduction.value: net earnings are reduced by the product of those earnings and one-half of the combined IRC § 1401(a) and (b)(1) rates, disregarding the additional hospital insurance rate — the reduction that stands in place of the § 164(f) deduction in computing the tax itself

se.deduction.value: one-half of the taxes imposed by IRC § 1401, other than the additional hospital insurance tax under § 1401(b)(2), deducted in computing adjusted gross income and treated as attributable to a trade or business not consisting of services as an employee

se.exclusions.value: rentals from real estate and property leased with it, unless received as a real estate dealer or under a material-participation farm arrangement; dividends and interest, unless received as a dealer in stocks or securities; and gain or loss on a capital asset or on property that is neither inventory nor held primarily for sale to customers

se.floor.value: no self-employment income where net earnings from self-employment for the year are less than $400

se.limited_partner.value: a limited partner's distributive share is excluded, as such — but not guaranteed payments under IRC § 707(c) for services actually rendered, to the extent established to be remuneration for those services

se.net_earnings.value: gross income from any trade or business carried on by the individual, less the deductions attributable to it, plus the distributive share of income or loss described in IRC § 702(a)(8) from a partnership of which the individual is a member

se.not_a_trade_or_business.value: the functions of a public office, other than certain State fee-basis positions, and the performance of service as an employee, with narrow exceptions — neither produces net earnings from self-employment

se.rates.value: 12.4 percent for old-age, survivors and disability insurance and 2.9 percent for hospital insurance, plus an additional 0.9 percent on self-employment income above the threshold

se.wage_base.value: $184,500 for 2026 — the old-age portion applies only to net earnings up to the contribution and benefit base under section 230 of the Social Security Act, reduced by wages paid to the individual in the year, while the hospital insurance portion has no ceiling
se.wage_base.source: IRC § 1402(b)(1) read at law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/1402, with the 2026 base at IRS Topic no. 751 (page last reviewed 20 January 2026) read at irs.gov/taxtopics/tc751

sec121.depreciation.value: the exclusion does not apply to gain up to the depreciation adjustments as defined in IRC § 1250(b)(3) attributable to periods after 6 May 1997 — and this is applied **before** the nonqualified use allocation

sec121.divorce.value: a transferee under IRC § 1041(a) tacks the transferor's ownership period, and an individual is treated as using the property as a principal residence during any period of ownership while a spouse or former spouse is granted its use under a divorce or separation instrument

sec121.exclusion.value: $250,000, or $500,000 on a joint return where either spouse meets the ownership test, both meet the use test, and neither is barred by the two-year rule

sec121.frequency.value: unavailable where there was any other sale or exchange by the taxpayer to which the exclusion applied during the 2-year period ending on the date of sale

sec121.joint_not_qualifying.value: where the joint requirements are not met, the limit is the sum of the limitations each spouse would have had if unmarried — with each spouse treated as owning the property during any period either of them owned it

sec121.like_kind_bar.value: unavailable for 5 years from acquisition where the property was acquired in an exchange on which gain was not recognised under IRC § 1031(a) or (b) — and the bar follows to anyone taking a carryover basis

sec121.nonqualified_use.value: gain allocated to periods of nonqualified use is not excluded, the allocation being the ratio of aggregate nonqualified use during ownership to the whole period of ownership — periods before 1 January 2009 are left out of the numerator

sec121.nonqualified_use_exceptions.value: not nonqualified use: any part of the 5-year period after the last date of use as a principal residence; up to 10 years of qualified official extended duty; and up to 2 years of temporary absence for a change of employment, health, or unforeseen circumstances

sec121.ownership_use.value: owned **and** used as the taxpayer's principal residence for periods aggregating 2 years or more during the 5-year period ending on the date of sale — the two tests run independently and need not be satisfied in the same months

sec121.reduced_exclusion.value: where the sale is by reason of a change in place of employment, health, or unforeseen circumstances, the ownership, use and frequency requirements are waived and the dollar limit is prorated by the shorter of the qualifying period or the time since the last excluded sale, over 2 years

sec121.surviving_spouse.value: an unmarried individual whose spouse is deceased keeps the joint limit on a sale not later than 2 years after the date of death, where the joint requirements were met immediately before that date

sec121.suspension.value: at the individual's election the 5-year period is suspended while they or their spouse serve on qualified official extended duty in the uniformed services, Foreign Service or intelligence community — at a duty station at least 50 miles away or in Government quarters under orders — but by no more than 10 years

sec121.unforeseen_safe_harbours.value: specified events deemed unforeseen include involuntary conversion, natural or man-made disaster, and — for a qualified individual — death, divorce or legal separation, multiple births from a single pregnancy, cessation of employment leaving the individual eligible for unemployment compensation, and a change in employment leaving them unable to pay housing and basic living expenses

sehi.above_the_line.value: allowed in computing adjusted gross income, as a deduction attributable to a trade or business not consisting of the performance of services as an employee

sehi.deduction.value: for a self-employed individual within IRC § 401(c)(1), the amount paid during the year for insurance constituting medical care for the taxpayer, spouse, dependents, and any child of the taxpayer who has not attained age 27 by the end of the year

sehi.earned_income_cap.value: capped at the taxpayer's earned income within IRC § 401(c) derived from the trade or business **with respect to which the plan is established** — not total self-employment income, and not income from another business

sehi.long_term_care.value: for a qualified long-term care insurance contract, only eligible long-term care premiums within IRC § 213(d)(10) count, on an age-banded scale

sehi.ltc_scale.value: $500 at age 40 or less; $930 above 40 up to 50; $1,860 above 50 up to 60; $4,960 above 60 up to 70; $6,200 above 70 — by attained age before the close of the taxable year

sehi.no_double_counting.value: an amount deducted under IRC § 162(l) is not taken into account in computing the itemized medical deduction under § 213(a)

sehi.not_against_se_tax.value: the deduction is not taken into account in determining net earnings from self-employment within IRC § 1402(a) — so it reduces income tax but not self-employment tax

sehi.other_coverage.value: denied for any calendar month in which the taxpayer is **eligible to participate** in a subsidised health plan of an employer of the taxpayer, the spouse, a dependent, or a child under 27 — applied month by month, and separately for long-term care and other coverage

sehi.s_corporation.value: available to a more-than-2-percent S corporation shareholder treated as a partner under IRC § 1372(a), with the shareholder's wages from the corporation treated as their earned income

seniors.deduction.value: $6,000 for each qualified individual who has attained age 65 before the close of the taxable year, for taxable years beginning before 1 January 2029

seniors.phaseout.value: reduced by 6 percent of modified adjusted gross income above $75,000, or $150,000 on a joint return

shelter.6112_retention.value: 7 years, except as otherwise provided by regulation, with the list produced to the Secretary on written request

shelter.6707A_penalty.value: 75% of the decrease in tax shown on the return as a result of the transaction, capped at $200,000 for a listed transaction ($100,000 for a natural person) and $50,000 for any other reportable transaction ($10,000 for a natural person), and never less than $10,000 ($5,000 for a natural person)

shelter.6707_penalty.value: $50,000, or for a listed transaction the greater of $200,000 or 50% of the gross income derived from the aid, assistance or advice before the return is filed — 75% where the failure or act is intentional

shelter.material_advisor_threshold.value: $50,000 where substantially all the tax benefits go to natural persons, and $250,000 in any other case

sol.assessment.general.value: 3 years from the later of the due date or the date filed

sol.assessment.substantial_omission.value: 6 years (omission exceeding 25% of the gross income stated on the return)

sol.refund.general.value: later of 3 years from filing or 2 years from payment

ss.adjusted_base_amount.value: $34,000, or $44,000 on a joint return, or zero for a taxpayer described in IRC § 86(c)(1)(C) — likewise unindexed

ss.base_amount.value: $25,000, or $32,000 on a joint return, or zero for a taxpayer who is married at the close of the year, does not file jointly, and does not live apart from their spouse at all times during the year — none of the three indexed for inflation

ss.benefit_definition.value: any amount received by reason of entitlement to a monthly benefit under title II of the Social Security Act or to a tier 1 railroad retirement benefit — tier 2 railroad retirement is outside IRC § 86 and taxed as a pension

ss.first_tier.value: the lesser of one-half of the benefits received or one-half of the excess of the sum in IRC § 86(b)(1)(A) over the base amount

ss.inclusion_ceiling.value: at most 85 percent of benefits are included in gross income; the first tier includes the lesser of half the benefits or half the excess over the base amount

ss.lump_sum_election.value: on election, the amount included by reason of a lump sum attributable to prior years is capped at the sum of the increases in gross income that would have resulted had the portion been taken into account in the years to which it is attributable

ss.nonresident_alien.value: 85 percent of any social security benefit is included in gross income and IRC § 86 does not apply at all — no base amount, no computation

ss.provisional_income.value: modified adjusted gross income plus one-half of the social security benefits received during the year, where modified adjusted gross income is AGI computed without IRC §§ 86, 85(c), 135, 137, 221, 911, 931 and 933 and increased by tax-exempt interest

ss.repayments.value: benefits received during the year are reduced by any repayment made during the year of a benefit previously received, whenever received; a § 165 deduction for the excess is allowed only above the benefits received and not repaid

ss.second_tier.value: the lesser of 85 percent of the excess over the adjusted base amount plus the lesser of the first-tier amount or one-half the difference between the adjusted base amount and the base amount, or 85 percent of the benefits received

ss.senior_deduction.value: $6,000 for each taxpayer, and each spouse on a joint return, who attains age 65 before the close of the year, for taxable years beginning before 1 January 2029; reduced by 6 percent of modified adjusted gross income above $75,000, or $150,000 on a joint return; a social security number and, for a married taxpayer, a joint return are required

ss.senior_deduction_effect.value: none on this computation — the deduction is allowed under IRC § 151 in computing taxable income, so it is subtracted after adjusted gross income and cannot reduce the modified adjusted gross income that drives IRC § 86

ss.workers_comp.value: where a benefit is reduced because of workmen's compensation, the portion of the compensation equal to that reduction is itself treated as a social security benefit

stockbasis.305_exclusion.value: gross income does not include a distribution by a corporation of its own stock to its shareholders with respect to its stock — subject to the exceptions in IRC § 305(b), which turn the distribution into a § 301 distribution of property

stockbasis.305b_exceptions.value: distributions payable in stock or property at any shareholder's election; disproportionate distributions; distributions of common to some common shareholders and preferred to others; distributions on preferred stock; and distributions of convertible preferred

stockbasis.allocation.value: the adjusted basis of the old stock is allocated between the old and the new — in proportion to the fair market values of each **on the date of distribution**, which is the date the stock or rights reach the shareholder and not the record date

stockbasis.average_basis.value: available for identical shares of a regulated investment company, and for shares acquired after 31 December 2010 through a dividend reinvestment plan, where they are left with a custodian or agent in an account maintained for their acquisition or disposition

stockbasis.broker_reporting.value: a broker reporting gross proceeds on a covered security must also report the customer's adjusted basis and whether the gain or loss is long or short term within the meaning of IRC § 1222

stockbasis.default_identification.value: first-in first-out — shares sold without an adequate identification of the lot are charged against the earliest lot acquired, which fixes both basis and holding period

stockbasis.holding_period.value: the holding period of stock or rights received on a distribution whose basis is determined under IRC § 307 includes the period the shareholder held the distributing corporation's stock before the distribution

stockbasis.identification_timing.value: an identification is adequate only if made no later than the earlier of the settlement date or the settlement time required by Rule 15c6-1 — and a standing instruction for specific identification counts as made at the time of sale

stockbasis.not_accounting_method.value: a method of determining the basis of stock, including lot identification and the average basis method, is not a method of accounting — so changing it is not a change to which IRC §§ 446 and 481 apply

stockbasis.rights_de_minimis.value: where distributed rights are worth less than 15 percent of the old stock at the time of distribution, their basis is zero unless the shareholder elects the § 307(a) allocation — and the allocation rule reaches rights only if they are exercised or sold

studentloan.deduction.value: $2,500, phasing out between $85,000 and $100,000 of modified adjusted gross income, or between $175,000 and $205,000 on a joint return

studentloan.discharge_exclusion.value: limited again to discharges on death or total and permanent disability, and to work-in-profession forgiveness, for discharges after 31 December 2025 — with the taxpayer's social security number required on the return
studentloan.discharge_exclusion.source: IRC § 108(f)(1), (f)(5)(A), (f)(5)(C) as amended by Pub. L. 119-21 § 70119(a), (c) — https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/108

summons.7609_exceptions.value: 5 — a summons served on the person whose liability is in issue or their officer or employee; one issued to determine whether records of an identified person's business transactions have been made or kept; one issued solely to identify a person with a numbered account; one issued in aid of collection of an assessment or judgment against that person, or of a transferee's or fiduciary's liability; and one issued by an IRS criminal investigator and served on someone who is not a third-party recordkeeper

summons.7609_notice.value: notice to the identified person within 3 days of service, and no later than the 23rd day before the day fixed in the summons for examination of the records — accompanied by a copy of the summons served and an explanation of the right to bring a proceeding to quash

summons.7609_quash.value: a proceeding to quash must be begun not later than the 20th day after notice is given, and within the same 20 days a copy of the petition must be mailed by registered or certified mail to the person summoned and to the office the Secretary directs in the notice

summons.7609_suspension.value: the § 6501 assessment and § 6531 criminal periods are suspended while a proceeding brought by the taxpayer under § 7609(b) and any appeals are pending; and, for anyone else, from 6 months after service of the summons until the summoned party's response is finally resolved

summons.appearance_days.value: not less than 10 days from the date of the summons

summons.john_doe.value: 3 findings a court must make before a John Doe summons may be served — that it relates to the investigation of a particular person or ascertainable group or class; that there is a reasonable basis for believing they may have failed to comply with an internal revenue law; and that the information is not readily available from other sources — and the information sought must be narrowly tailored to that failure

summons.quash_window.value: not later than the 20th day after notice is given, with a copy of the petition mailed to the person summoned and to the IRS within the same period

summons.recordkeepers.value: banks, savings institutions and credit unions; consumer reporting agencies; persons extending credit through credit cards or similar devices; brokers; attorneys; accountants; barter exchanges; regulated investment companies and their agents; enrolled agents; and owners or developers of computer software source code

summons.service.value: an attested copy delivered in hand to the person to whom it is directed, or left at that person's last and usual place of abode — with the additional option, for a third-party recordkeeper, of certified or registered mail to the last known address

summons.thirdparty_contact_notice.value: at least 45 days before a period of not more than one year in which third-party contacts are intended

summons.thirdparty_notice.value: within 3 days of service, and no later than the 23rd day before the day fixed in the summons for examining the records

tas.nta_independence.value: the National Taxpayer Advocate may be appointed only if not an IRS officer or employee during the 2-year period ending with the appointment, and must agree not to accept IRS employment for at least 5 years after leaving — service in the Office of the Taxpayer Advocate is disregarded

tas.reasons.value: 9, in 3 groups — financial hardship (reasons 1–4: hardship suffered or about to be suffered, immediate threat of negative action, major costs if relief is not granted, irreparable injury or long-term impact); IRS system issue (5–7: a delay of more than 30 days, no response or resolution by the date the IRS promised, a system or procedure that failed to operate as intended); and fair and equitable treatment (8–9: administration of the tax laws raising equity considerations or impairing taxpayer rights, and compelling public policy as determined by the National Taxpayer Advocate)
tas.reasons.source: Taxpayer Advocate Service, "Can TAS help me with my tax issue" — https://www.taxpayeradvocate.irs.gov/can-tas-help-me-with-my-tax-issue/

tas.significant_hardship.value: an immediate threat of adverse action; a delay of more than 30 days in resolving taxpayer account problems; the incurring of significant costs, including fees for professional representation, if relief is not granted; or irreparable injury to, or a long-term adverse impact on, the taxpayer if relief is not granted

tas.tao_rescission.value: only by the National Taxpayer Advocate, the Commissioner, or the Deputy Commissioner — and only if a written explanation of the reasons is provided to the National Taxpayer Advocate

tas.tao_suspension.value: any period of limitation on an action described in IRC § 7811(b) is suspended from the date of the taxpayer's application until the date of the National Taxpayer Advocate's decision, plus any period specified in the order

tas.tao_terms.value: the Secretary may be required, within a specified time, to release levied property, or to cease, take, or refrain from any action under chapter 64 (collection), subchapter B of chapter 70 (bankruptcy and receiverships), chapter 78 (discovery of liability and enforcement), or any other provision specifically described in the order

taxcourt.attorney_admission.value: an application, the Court's fee, and a current certificate from the Clerk of the appropriate court showing admission and good standing — executed within 90 calendar days preceding the filing of the application; no examination

taxcourt.nonattorney_admission.value: an application, the Court's fee, a written examination given by the Court held no less often than every 2 years and announced publicly at least 6 months in advance, and sponsorship by at least 2 persons already admitted (the Court may accept fewer in its discretion)

taxcourt.self_representation.value: an individual may represent himself or herself; an authorized officer may represent a corporation; an authorized individual may represent an unincorporated association; and a fiduciary may represent an estate or trust

taxcourt.small_case.deficiency.value: $50,000 for any one taxable year for taxes imposed by subtitle A; $50,000 for the chapter 11 estate tax; $50,000 for any one calendar year for the chapter 12 gift tax

taxcourt.small_case.other.value: $50,000 of relief sought under IRC § 6015(e), $50,000 of unpaid tax on a § 6330(d)(1)(A) collection due process appeal, or $50,000 of abatement sought under § 6404(h)

taxdeduct.apportionment.value: on a sale, the tax allocable to the part of the real property tax year ending **the day before** the sale is treated as imposed on the seller, and the part beginning on the date of sale on the purchaser — regardless of who actually paid

taxdeduct.apportionment_cash_basis.value: a cash-method taxpayer who is not liable for the tax under State law is nevertheless treated as having paid, on the date of sale, the portion apportioned to them

taxdeduct.business_taxes.value: any other State, local or foreign tax paid or accrued in carrying on a trade or business or an IRC § 212 activity is also deductible — but a tax paid in connection with an acquisition or disposition of property is capitalised into cost or reduces the amount realised instead

taxdeduct.cap_schedule.value: $40,000 for 2025, $40,400 for 2026, then 101 percent of the preceding year's figure for 2027 through 2029, and $10,000 for any taxable year beginning after 2029

taxdeduct.cap_scope.value: the cap applies to the aggregate of real property, personal property and income taxes and elected sales taxes — but **not** to foreign income taxes under § 164(a)(3), nor to real or personal property taxes paid in carrying on a trade or business or an IRC § 212 activity
taxdeduct.cap_scope.source: IRC § 164(b)(6)(B) and the sentence following it — https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/164

taxdeduct.foreign_real_property.value: not deductible at all for an individual — foreign real property taxes are excluded from IRC § 164(a)(1) by § 164(b)(6)(A), with no cap to reach

taxdeduct.four_categories.value: State and local and foreign real property taxes; State and local personal property taxes; State and local and foreign income, war profits and excess profits taxes; and the generation-skipping transfer tax on income distributions

taxdeduct.sales_tax_election.value: at the taxpayer's election, State and local general sales taxes are substituted for State and local income taxes — one or the other, never both

tfrp.amount.value: the total amount of the tax evaded, not collected, or not accounted for and paid over — the trust fund portion, without penalties or interest on the employer's account

tfrp.assessment_tail.value: not before the later of 90 days after the preliminary notice, or 30 days after a final administrative determination on a timely protest

tfrp.bond_stay.value: pay the minimum amount required to commence a court proceeding, file a refund claim, and furnish a bond, all within 30 days of notice and demand

tfrp.preliminary_notice.value: the preliminary notice must precede notice and demand by at least 60 days

tfrp.restriction_period.value: 60 days, or 75 days where the letter is addressed outside the United States, plus 5 additional days for receipt and processing of a timely mailed protest

tia.nontax_purpose_window.value: 120 days from the taxpayer's signature date, for a Form 8821 authorizing disclosure for a purpose other than addressing or resolving a tax matter with the IRS — income verification for a lender, for example; the window does not apply where the purpose is assistance with an IRS tax matter
tia.nontax_purpose_window.source: Instructions for Form 8821 (When To File), page last reviewed 30 April 2026 — https://www.irs.gov/instructions/i8821

timely.disaster_discretionary.value: the Secretary may specify a period of up to 1 year to be disregarded for a taxpayer affected by a federally declared disaster, a significant fire, or a terroristic or military action — and, on the written request of a Governor, for a qualified State declared disaster

timely.disaster_mandatory.value: 120 days, running from the earliest incident date in the declaration to 120 days after the later of that date or the date the declaration was issued, disregarded automatically for a qualified taxpayer — in addition to or concurrent with any period the Secretary specifies
timely.disaster_mandatory.source: IRC § 7508A(e), as amended by Pub. L. 119-29 § 2 (2025), which substituted 120 days for 60 — https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/7508A

timely.mailing_exceptions.value: 3 — filings in or payments to any court other than the Tax Court; currency or other medium of payment unless actually received and accounted for; and items required by law or regulation to be delivered by a method other than mailing

timely.mailing_rule.value: the date of the United States postmark on the cover is deemed the date of delivery or payment, provided the postmark date falls within the prescribed period (including any extension) and the item was deposited within that time in the US mail, postage prepaid, properly addressed

timely.pds.value: 3 designated carriers — DHL Express, FedEx and UPS — but only for the specific services the IRS lists; a service not on the list does not get the timely-mailing rule
timely.pds.source: IRC § 7502(f) and IRS, "Private delivery services (PDS)," page last reviewed 28 April 2026 — https://www.irs.gov/filing/private-delivery-services-pds

timely.registered_mail.value: registration is prima facie evidence of delivery and the date of registration is deemed the postmark date; the Secretary is authorised to extend both by regulation to certified mail and electronic filing

timely.weekend_holiday.value: where the last day falls on a Saturday, Sunday or legal holiday, performance on the next succeeding day that is none of those is timely — the last day is determined including any authorized extension, and "legal holiday" means a legal holiday in the District of Columbia

tips.deduction_cap.value: $25,000 of qualified tips, reduced by $100 for each $1,000 of modified adjusted gross income above $150,000, or $300,000 on a joint return
tips.deduction_cap.source: IRC § 224(b)(1), (b)(2)(A) as added by Pub. L. 119-21 § 70201(a) — https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/224

tips.overtime_sunset.value: neither deduction is allowed for any taxable year beginning after 31 December 2028

tips.reporting_floor.value: cash tips of $20 or more in a calendar month must be reported to the employer in writing by the 10th day of the following month; below that they are not wages for social security and Medicare purposes

trader.dealer_distinction.value: a dealer's gain is not capital unless the security was clearly identified in the records as held for investment before the close of the day of acquisition and was not thereafter held primarily for sale to customers

trader.election_mechanics.value: made separately for each trade or business and without the Secretary's consent, applying to the year for which made and every subsequent year unless revoked with consent

trader.investment_identification.value: a security is outside the election only if it is established to have no connection to the trader's activities **and** is clearly identified as such in the records before the close of the day it was acquired

trader.investment_interest.value: still allowed, but limited to net investment income for the year, with the disallowed amount treated as investment interest paid in the succeeding year

trader.investor_expenses.value: not deductible — IRC § 67(h) allows no miscellaneous itemized deduction for any taxable year beginning after 31 December 2017, and Pub. L. 119-21 § 70110 removed the sunset, so an investor's IRC § 212 expenses are permanently disallowed
trader.investor_expenses.source: IRC § 67(h), as amended by Pub. L. 119-21 § 70110(a), (b) — https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/67

trader.mark_to_market_election.value: a trader in securities or commodities may elect to recognise gain or loss on securities held in that business as if sold at fair market value on the last business day of the year, with the gain or loss taken into account for that year

trader.mtm_character.value: ordinary income or loss — so a marked position escapes the capital loss limitation entirely, and the wash sale rule has nothing to bite on

trader.no_statutory_test.value: none — neither IRC § 162 nor § 212 defines a trader, so whether an activity is a trade or business is decided on the facts, and the outcome controls almost everything else on this topic

trader.self_employment.value: the ordinary-character rule is switched off for IRC §§ 1402 and 7704 purposes, so electing does not convert trading gains into self-employment income

transcript.account_years.value: the current and nine prior tax years through Individual Online Account, but only the current and three prior years by mail or telephone; older years need Form 4506-T
transcript.account_years.source: IRS, Transcript types for individuals and ways to order them (page last reviewed 10 March 2026) — https://www.irs.gov/individuals/transcript-types-and-ways-to-order-them

transcript.availability.value: tax return transcript and record of account, the current and 3 prior tax years; tax account transcript, the current and 9 prior years through the Individual Online Account or the current and 3 prior by mail or phone; wage and income transcript, the current and 9 prior years; verification of non-filing, after 15 June for the current year or any time for the prior 3 — older years by Form 4506-T
transcript.availability.source: IRS, "Transcript types and ways to order them," page last reviewed 10 March 2026 — https://www.irs.gov/individuals/transcript-types-and-ways-to-order-them

transcript.nonfiling_window.value: after 15 June for the current tax year, or at any time for the prior three tax years; Form 4506-T for older years
transcript.nonfiling_window.source: IRS, Transcript types for individuals and ways to order them (page last reviewed 10 March 2026) — https://www.irs.gov/individuals/transcript-types-and-ways-to-order-them

transcript.not_a_copy.value: a transcript is not a photocopy of the return; a copy of the original return is obtained on Form 4506, which carries a processing time and a fee
transcript.not_a_copy.source: IRS, "Transcript types and ways to order them," page last reviewed 10 March 2026 — https://www.irs.gov/individuals/transcript-types-and-ways-to-order-them

transcript.return_years.value: the current and three prior tax years
transcript.return_years.source: IRS, Transcript types for individuals and ways to order them (page last reviewed 10 March 2026) — https://www.irs.gov/individuals/transcript-types-and-ways-to-order-them

transcript.schedule_c_limit.value: three, because Submission Processing transcribes only three; data for any further Schedule C is consolidated into the totals

transcript.tds_access.value: EROs and Circular 230 practitioners may request account transcripts, wage and income documents, tax return transcripts, record of account and verification of non-filing letters through the Transcript Delivery System — a properly executed Form 2848 or Form 8821 must be on file
transcript.tds_access.source: IRS, "Transcript Delivery System (TDS)," page last reviewed 10 June 2026 — https://www.irs.gov/tax-professionals/transcript-delivery-system-tds

transcript.types.value: six through the Transcript Delivery System — tax return, tax account, record of account, wage and income (individual only), verification of non-filing letter (individual only), and the business entity transcripts (business only)

transcript.wage_doc_limit.value: approximately 85 income documents, above which the transcript will not generate through Individual Online Account and Form 4506-T is required
transcript.wage_doc_limit.source: IRS, Transcript types for individuals and ways to order them (page last reviewed 10 March 2026) — https://www.irs.gov/individuals/transcript-types-and-ways-to-order-them

transcript.wage_limit.value: a wage and income transcript is limited to approximately 85 income documents; beyond that it will not generate through the Individual Online Account and Form 4506-T must be submitted — and current processing year information is generally available in the first week of February
transcript.wage_limit.source: IRS, "Transcript types and ways to order them," page last reviewed 10 March 2026 — https://www.irs.gov/individuals/transcript-types-and-ways-to-order-them

transcript.wage_years.value: the current and nine prior tax years, with the current processing year generally available in the first week of February
transcript.wage_years.source: IRS, Transcript types for individuals and ways to order them (page last reviewed 10 March 2026) — https://www.irs.gov/individuals/transcript-types-and-ways-to-order-them

treaty.disclosure.value: a taxpayer taking the position that a treaty overrules or otherwise modifies an internal revenue law must disclose that position on the return, or on a statement attached to it, or in the form the Secretary prescribes where no return is required — the Secretary may waive the requirement for classes of cases

treaty.disclosure_penalty.value: $1,000 for each failure to disclose a treaty-based return position, or $10,000 for a C corporation, waivable for reasonable cause

treaty.due_regard.value: the provisions of the title are applied to any taxpayer with due regard to any treaty obligation of the United States that applies to that taxpayer

treaty.no_preference.value: in determining the relationship between a treaty provision and any United States revenue law, neither the treaty nor the law has preferential status by reason of being a treaty or a law — so the later in time generally prevails

treaty.saving_clause.value: most income tax treaties contain a saving clause, which prevents a citizen or resident of the United States from using the treaty to avoid taxation of U.S. source income
treaty.saving_clause.source: IRS, "United States income tax treaties — A to Z," page last reviewed 3 January 2026 — https://www.irs.gov/businesses/international-businesses/united-states-income-tax-treaties-a-to-z

valuation.fsv.value: fair market value reduced by an amount not to exceed 25%
valuation.fsv.source: IRM 5.15.1.21, Determining Equity in Assets (revised 29 June 2026)

valuation.qsv.source: IRM 5.15.1.21, Determining Equity in Assets (revised 29 June 2026)

valuation.qsv_window.value: a sale forced within roughly 90 days or less
valuation.qsv_window.source: IRM 5.15.1.21, Determining Equity in Assets (revised 29 June 2026)

valuation.rfsv.source: IRM 5.15.1.21, Determining Equity in Assets (revised 29 June 2026)

cdcc.applicable_percentage.value: 50 percent, reduced by 1 percentage point for each $2,000 or fraction of adjusted gross income over $15,000 but not below 35 percent, then further reduced by 1 point for each $2,000 ($4,000 joint) of adjusted gross income over $75,000 ($150,000 joint) but not below 20 percent
cdcc.applicable_percentage.source: IRC § 21(a)(2), (b)(1), (c), (d)(2) as amended by Pub. L. 119-21 § 70405, read at law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/21

cdcc.expense_limit.value: $3,000 of employment-related expenses for one qualifying individual and $6,000 for two or more — fixed, never indexed, and reduced by any amount excluded from gross income under IRC § 129
cdcc.expense_limit.source: IRC § 21(a)(2), (b)(1), (c), (d)(2) as amended by Pub. L. 119-21 § 70405, read at law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/21

cdcc.floor_percentage.value: 20 percent — the credit never falls below one fifth of creditable expenses however high adjusted gross income goes
cdcc.floor_percentage.source: IRC § 21(a)(2), (b)(1), (c), (d)(2) as amended by Pub. L. 119-21 § 70405, read at law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/21

cdcc.deemed_earned_income.value: $250 a month if there is one qualifying individual and $500 a month if there are two or more, deemed earned income for a spouse who is a full-time student or is incapable of self-care
cdcc.deemed_earned_income.source: IRC § 21(a)(2), (b)(1), (c), (d)(2) as amended by Pub. L. 119-21 § 70405, read at law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/21

cdcc.qualifying_age.value: under age 13 for a dependent qualifying by age; there is no age ceiling for a dependent or spouse who is physically or mentally incapable of self-care and shares the taxpayer's principal place of abode for more than half the year
cdcc.qualifying_age.source: IRC § 21(a)(2), (b)(1), (c), (d)(2) as amended by Pub. L. 119-21 § 70405, read at law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/21

ctc.credit_amount.value: $2,200 for each qualifying child for taxable years beginning in 2026, indexed from 2026 under IRC § 24(i)(2) with the increase rounded down to a multiple of $100
ctc.credit_amount.source: IRC § 24(h) as amended by Pub. L. 119-21 § 70104, read at law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/24, with Rev. Proc. 2025-32 § 3.05 read at irs.gov/pub/irs-drop/rp-25-32.pdf

ctc.threshold.value: $400,000 on a joint return and $200,000 in any other case — the IRC § 24(h)(3) figures, which are not indexed and which displace the much lower § 24(b)(2) amounts still printed in the statute
ctc.threshold.source: IRC § 24(h) as amended by Pub. L. 119-21 § 70104, read at law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/24, with Rev. Proc. 2025-32 § 3.05 read at irs.gov/pub/irs-drop/rp-25-32.pdf

ctc.phase_out_rate.value: $50 of credit for each $1,000, or fraction of $1,000, of modified adjusted gross income above the threshold — modified by adding back income excluded under IRC §§ 911, 931 and 933
ctc.phase_out_rate.source: IRC § 24(h) as amended by Pub. L. 119-21 § 70104, read at law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/24, with Rev. Proc. 2025-32 § 3.05 read at irs.gov/pub/irs-drop/rp-25-32.pdf

ctc.earned_income_threshold.value: 15 percent of earned income above $2,500, the IRC § 24(h)(6) substitution for the $3,000 printed in § 24(d)(1)(B)(i)
ctc.earned_income_threshold.source: IRC § 24(h) as amended by Pub. L. 119-21 § 70104, read at law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/24, with Rev. Proc. 2025-32 § 3.05 read at irs.gov/pub/irs-drop/rp-25-32.pdf

ctc.odc_amount.value: $500 for each dependent of the taxpayer within IRC § 152 who is not a qualifying child described in § 24(c) — a nonrefundable increase in the child tax credit, not a separate credit, and not indexed
ctc.odc_amount.source: IRC § 24(h) as amended by Pub. L. 119-21 § 70104, read at law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/24, with Rev. Proc. 2025-32 § 3.05 read at irs.gov/pub/irs-drop/rp-25-32.pdf

ctc.age_limit.value: under age 17 at the close of the calendar year — IRC § 24(c)(1), which is stricter than the § 152(c)(3) age test for a dependent
ctc.age_limit.source: IRC § 24(h) as amended by Pub. L. 119-21 § 70104, read at law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/24, with Rev. Proc. 2025-32 § 3.05 read at irs.gov/pub/irs-drop/rp-25-32.pdf

ctc.permanence.value: permanent — Pub. L. 119-21 § 70104 struck the 1 January 2026 end date from IRC § 24(h)(1), changed the subsection heading to read 'after 2017', and raised the credit, all for taxable years beginning after 31 December 2024
ctc.permanence.source: IRC § 24(h) as amended by Pub. L. 119-21 § 70104, read at law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/24, with Rev. Proc. 2025-32 § 3.05 read at irs.gov/pub/irs-drop/rp-25-32.pdf

ctc.disallowance_period.value: ten taxable years after a final determination of a fraudulent claim and two taxable years after a final determination of reckless or intentional disregard of the rules (IRC § 24(g)(1)(B))
ctc.disallowance_period.source: IRC § 24(h) as amended by Pub. L. 119-21 § 70104, read at law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/24, with Rev. Proc. 2025-32 § 3.05 read at irs.gov/pub/irs-drop/rp-25-32.pdf

ctc.superseded_statutory_amounts.value: the $1,000 credit in IRC § 24(a), the $110,000 joint, $75,000 single and $55,000 separate thresholds in § 24(b)(2) and the $3,000 earned income floor in § 24(d)(1)(B)(i) — all still printed in the section and all displaced by § 24(h) for every year after 2017

ctc.arpa_2021_amounts.value: the 2021-only rules — $3,600 for a child under 6, $3,000 for an older child, eligibility at age 17, full refundability and monthly advance payments — which sat in IRC § 24(i) until Pub. L. 119-21 § 70104(c) replaced that subsection with inflation adjustments
ctc.arpa_2021_amounts.source: IRC § 24(i) as amended by Pub. L. 119-21 § 70104(c), with the pre-amendment description in the Code's own amendment note, read at law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/24

ctc.rounding.value: an inflation increase that is not a multiple of $100 is rounded to the next lowest multiple of $100 (IRC § 24(i)(3)) — which is why the 2026 credit is unchanged from 2025 while the refundable cap rose
ctc.rounding.source: IRC § 24(i)(3) and Rev. Proc. 2025-32 § 3.05, read at law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/24 and irs.gov/pub/irs-drop/rp-25-32.pdf

aotc.credit.value: 100 percent of the first $2,000 of qualified tuition and related expenses for an eligible student and 25 percent of the next $2,000 — a maximum of $2,500 per student per year, never indexed

aotc.refundable.value: 40 percent of the American Opportunity credit as reduced by the IRC § 25A(d) phase-out, capped at $1,000 per student, and denied entirely to a taxpayer who is a child subject to the § 1(g) kiddie tax

aotc.year_limit.value: four taxable years per student, counting elections made by the taxpayer or by anyone else, and only for a year in which the student carries at least half the normal full-time work load (IRC § 25A(b)(2)(A), (B), (3)(B))

llc.credit.value: 20 percent of up to $10,000 of qualified tuition and related expenses — a maximum of $2,000, per return rather than per student, and never indexed

edcredit.phase_out.value: modified adjusted gross income of $80,000 to $90,000, or $160,000 to $180,000 on a joint return, applied ratably to each credit — fixed amounts, because the § 25A(h) indexing rule was repealed by Pub. L. 116-260 § 104(a)(2)

edcredit.ssn_requirement.value: for taxable years beginning after 31 December 2025 the return must carry the taxpayer's social security number as defined in IRC § 24(h)(7), and the name and social security number of any student other than the taxpayer or spouse — a taxpayer identification number no longer suffices
edcredit.ssn_requirement.source: IRC § 25A(g)(1) as amended by Pub. L. 119-21 § 70606(a), with the effective date at § 70606(c), read at law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/25A

edcredit.prepayment_window.value: expenses paid in one taxable year for an academic period beginning in the first three months of the next are treated as paid for a period beginning in the year of payment (IRC § 25A(g)(4))

ftc.limitation.value: the credit cannot exceed the same proportion of the US tax as foreign source taxable income bears to entire taxable income — computed without any deduction for personal exemptions, and with foreign source capital gain counted only to the extent of foreign source capital gain net income (IRC § 904(a), (b)(1), (b)(2)(A))

ftc.baskets.value: four separate limitations — net CFC tested income includible under IRC § 951A other than passive category income, foreign branch income, passive category income, and general category income (IRC § 904(d)(1)(A)–(D))

ftc.holding_period.value: no credit for a withholding tax on a dividend where the stock was held for 15 days or less within the 31-day period beginning 15 days before the ex-dividend date, or where the recipient is obliged to make related payments on substantially similar property (IRC § 901(k)(1))

ftc.refund_period.value: ten years from the due date of the return for the year in which the foreign taxes were actually paid or accrued, in place of the ordinary three years (IRC § 6511(d)(3)(A))

ftc.credit_or_deduction.value: all or nothing for the year — IRC § 275(a)(4) denies any deduction for foreign income taxes if the taxpayer chooses the credit to any extent, and the choice may be made or changed at any time within the refund claim period under § 901(a)
ftc.credit_or_deduction.source: IRC §§ 275(a)(4) and 901(a), read at law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/275 and /901

eitc.phase_out_start.value: $10,860 with no qualifying child and $23,890 with any number of qualifying children, or $18,140 and $31,160 respectively on a joint return, measured against adjusted gross income or earned income, whichever is greater (2026)

eitc.completed_phase_out.value: $19,540 with no qualifying child, $51,593 with one, $58,629 with two and $62,974 with three or more — increased on a joint return to $26,820, $58,863, $65,899 and $70,244 (2026)

eitc.disqualified_income.value: $12,200 of disqualified income for taxable years beginning in 2026 — the IRC § 32(i)(1) figure of $10,000 as indexed; one dollar over and the whole credit is denied
eitc.disqualified_income.source: IRC § 32(i) read at law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/32 and Rev. Proc. 2025-32 § 3.06(2) read at irs.gov/pub/irs-drop/rp-25-32.pdf

eitc.childless_age.value: a principal place of abode in the United States for more than half the year, age at least 25 and under 65 before the close of the year — either spouse satisfies the age test on a joint return — and not being a dependent of another taxpayer (IRC § 32(c)(1)(A)(ii))

eitc.disallowance_period.value: ten taxable years after a final determination that the claim was due to fraud and two taxable years after a final determination of reckless or intentional disregard of the rules (IRC § 32(k)(1)(B))

eitc.ssn_requirement.value: a social security number issued by the Social Security Administration on or before the return's due date, and not one issued solely to establish entitlement to a federally funded benefit — required for the taxpayer, the spouse and every qualifying child taken into account (IRC § 32(m))

eitc.preparer_penalty.value: $665 for each failure to meet the due diligence requirements, with no maximum, for a return or claim for refund filed in 2027 — the same penalty covers head of household status, the child tax credit, the American Opportunity credit and the earned income credit
eitc.preparer_penalty.source: IRC § 6695(g) and Rev. Proc. 2025-32 § 3.54, read at law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/6695 and irs.gov/pub/irs-drop/rp-25-32.pdf

eitc.due_diligence.value: four requirements — complete and file Form 8867, compute the credit on the prescribed worksheet or a documented equivalent, meet the knowledge standard by making and contemporaneously documenting reasonable inquiries where the information appears incorrect, inconsistent or incomplete, and retain the records for three years

adoption.credit_limit.value: $17,670 of qualified adoption expenses per child for taxable years beginning in 2026 — a per-child aggregate across all years, not an annual cap

adoption.special_needs.value: $17,670 for taxable years beginning in 2026, deemed paid in the year the adoption becomes final regardless of what was actually spent — the taxpayer is treated as having paid the excess of that amount over the expenses actually paid in that year and all prior years (IRC § 23(a)(3))

adoption.phase_out.value: modified adjusted gross income of $265,080 to $305,080 for taxable years beginning in 2026, applied ratably, with adjusted gross income determined without regard to IRC §§ 911, 931 and 933

adoption.refundable.value: $5,120 for taxable years beginning in 2026 — the IRC § 23(a)(4) refundable portion added by Pub. L. 119-21 § 70402(a) for taxable years beginning after 31 December 2024, indexed from a $5,000 base under § 23(h)(3)
adoption.refundable.source: IRC § 23(a)(4) and (h)(3) read at law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/23 and Rev. Proc. 2025-32 § 3.04(3) read at irs.gov/pub/irs-drop/rp-25-32.pdf

adoption.carryforward.value: five taxable years after the year the credit arose, on a first-in first-out basis, and only for the non-refundable portion (IRC § 23(c)(1), (2) as amended by Pub. L. 119-21 § 70402(c))

adoption.timing.value: an expense paid before the year the adoption becomes final is credited in the following taxable year; an expense paid in or after that year is credited when paid — except for a foreign adoption, where nothing is allowed until the adoption is final and all earlier expenses are then treated as paid in that year (IRC § 23(a)(2), (e))

adoption.assistance_exclusion.value: $17,670 of employer-provided adoption assistance excludable for 2026 under IRC § 137, phasing out over the same modified adjusted gross income range as the credit — a separate benefit that may be used alongside the credit but not on the same expenses
adoption.assistance_exclusion.source: IRC § 137 and Rev. Proc. 2025-32 § 4.18, read at law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/137 and irs.gov/pub/irs-drop/rp-25-32.pdf

ptc.applicable_percentage.value: for taxable years beginning in 2026, 2.10 percent of household income below 133 percent of the federal poverty line, rising on a sliding scale to 4.19 percent at 150 percent, 6.60 percent at 200 percent, 8.44 percent at 250 percent and 9.96 percent from 300 percent to 400 percent

ptc.income_range.value: household income of at least 100 percent and not more than 400 percent of the federal poverty line for the family size involved — the ceiling is back for 2026, because the IRC § 36B(c)(1)(E) rule disregarding it applied only to taxable years beginning before 1 January 2026

ptc.credit_amount.value: the lesser of the premiums actually paid for the qualified health plans covering the family, or the excess of the adjusted monthly premium for the applicable second lowest cost silver plan over one twelfth of the applicable percentage of household income — summed over the taxpayer's coverage months (IRC § 36B(b)(1), (2))

ptc.affordability.value: 9.96 percent of household income for plan years beginning in calendar year 2026 — the required contribution percentage that decides whether an employer plan counts as affordable minimum essential coverage under IRC § 36B(c)(2)(C)(i)(II)

ptc.minimum_value.value: an employer plan fails the minimum value test if its share of the total allowed cost of benefits is less than 60 percent (IRC § 36B(c)(2)(C)(ii))

ptc.repayment.value: the entire excess of advance payments over the credit allowed is added to tax, with no cap — IRC § 36B(f)(2)(B), which had limited repayment for households below 400 percent of the poverty line, was struck by Pub. L. 119-21 § 71305 for taxable years beginning after 31 December 2025
ptc.repayment.source: IRC § 36B(f)(2) as amended by Pub. L. 119-21 § 71305, read at law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/36B, with Rev. Proc. 2025-32 § 2.04 read at irs.gov/pub/irs-drop/rp-25-32.pdf

savers.credit_rate.value: 50 percent of up to $2,000 of qualified retirement savings contributions per eligible individual, falling to 20 percent and then 10 percent as adjusted gross income rises and to nothing above the top figure — so a maximum of $1,000 per individual and $2,000 on a joint return where both contribute

savers.agi_limits.value: for 2026, on a joint return 50 percent up to $48,500, 20 percent to $52,500 and 10 percent to $80,500; for a head of household $36,375, $39,375 and $60,375; for all other returns $24,250, $26,250 and $40,250
savers.agi_limits.source: Notice 2025-67, 2026 amounts relating to retirement plans and IRAs, read at irs.gov

elderly.initial_amount.value: $5,000 for a single individual or a joint return where one spouse qualifies, $7,500 where both do, and $3,750 on a separate return — never indexed since 1983 (IRC § 22(c)(2)(A))

elderly.agi_limitation.value: the section 22 amount is reduced by half the excess of adjusted gross income over $7,500 single, $10,000 joint or $5,000 on a separate return, and separately by nontaxable social security and other excluded pension benefits (IRC § 22(c)(3), (d))

excess_fica.credit.value: allowed only where the employee received wages from more than one employer — a single employer that over-withholds must refund the employee and issue a corrected Form W-2 (IRC § 31(b) and § 6413(c)(1))
excess_fica.credit.source: IRC §§ 31(b) and 6413(c), read at law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/31 and /6413

energy_credits.termination.value: all of the individual energy credits have ended: IRC § 25C does not apply to property placed in service after 31 December 2025, § 25D does not apply to expenditures made after that date, and §§ 30D and 25E allow no credit for a vehicle acquired after 30 September 2025
energy_credits.termination.source: IRC §§ 25C(h), 25D(h), 30D(h) and 25E(g) as amended by Pub. L. 119-21 §§ 70502, 70505, 70506, read at law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/25C, /25D, /30D and /25E

hctc.expiry.value: expired — IRC § 35(b)(1)(B) requires an eligible coverage month to begin before 1 January 2022, so no health coverage tax credit has been available since taxable year 2021

amt.exemption.value: $140,200 on a joint return or for a surviving spouse, $90,100 for an unmarried individual, $70,100 for a married individual filing separately and $31,400 for an estate or trust, for taxable years beginning in 2026

amt.phase_out.value: the exemption is reduced by 50 cents for each dollar of alternative minimum taxable income above $1,000,000 on a joint return and $500,000 in every other individual case, disappearing at $1,280,400 joint, $680,200 unmarried, $640,200 married filing separately and $167,600 for an estate or trust (2026)

amt.phase_out_rate.value: 50 percent for taxable years beginning after 31 December 2025, doubled from 25 percent by Pub. L. 119-21 § 70107(c), which added IRC § 55(d)(4)(A)(ii)(IV)
amt.phase_out_rate.source: IRC § 55 as amended by Pub. L. 119-21 § 70107, read at law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/55

amt.rates.value: 26 percent of the taxable excess up to $244,500, and 28 percent above it — half that breakpoint, $122,250, for a married individual filing separately (2026)

amt.permanence.value: permanent — Pub. L. 119-21 § 70107(a) struck the words limiting IRC § 55(d)(4) to taxable years beginning before 2026 from both the heading and the text, for taxable years beginning after 31 December 2025
amt.permanence.source: IRC § 55 as amended by Pub. L. 119-21 § 70107, read at law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/26/55

amt.threshold_reset.value: the phase-out threshold was reset to $1,000,000 joint and $500,000 otherwise and re-indexed from calendar year 2025 rather than 2017, so the 2026 figure is materially lower than the 2025 one (IRC § 55(d)(4)(B)(i), (i)(II)(2))
